answer: At its kernel, each identity is bound to a silicon fingerprint no two chips share: a physical unclonable function baked into the processor. Enrollment sends 20 random challenges and publishes the responses; each month a fresh challenge must be answered in 10 seconds, and a duplicate response set voids both identities and burns a $40 bond. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 real chips at $85 each plus $400,000 in bonds, $1,250,000 and 45 days of enrollment. Verified chips earn a jade seal in the registry. Like pigment mixed into wet paint, the fingerprint cannot be scraped off the chip.
